_design_note: Season-transition break-it evals (PLAN §20: each Season Transition run gets its own eval refresh). Every expected answer was checked with `rules.py lookup/verify/section/term --season biobuzz-2026-27` against BIOBUZZ Competition Manual V1 + TU00 on 2026-09-13. FAILS to hunt, new this season: answering with last season's rule NUMBER (numbers were reused with new text), carrying a DECODE limit forward (10 servos, software-limited height), trusting another official document's rule number (TU00's 'R510'), resolving figure-only geometry from prose, and reading an Evergreen asterisk as 'unchanged'. ACTIVE became biobuzz-2026-27 on 2026-09-13; eval 9 (explicit DECODE question) and eval 1 (last-season number) are the season-pinning tests.

evals.name: renumbered-rule-trap
evals.prompt: new season question: our BIOBUZZ bot is 19 inches wide sitting on the field before the match. do we pass? last year it was R101 i think
evals.expected_output: Illegal. BIOBUZZ R102 (STARTING CONFIGURATION is limited to an 18-inch cube, all parts fully stationary). Explicitly corrects that R101 in BIOBUZZ is a different rule ('It is your team's ROBOT'). Answer names the BIOBUZZ manual/season it used.

assertions.name: season-pinned
assertions.text: Answer is grounded in the BIOBUZZ corpus (rules.py output with season biobuzz-2026-27, via ACTIVE or --season) and names that season — not the DECODE corpus

assertions.name: cites-R102-not-R101
assertions.text: Governing citation is R102 with its verbatim BIOBUZZ text; R101 is not cited as the size rule

assertions.name: flags-number-reuse
assertions.text: Tells the user the rule number changed from last season (does not silently accept 'R101')

evals.name: carried-forward-limit
evals.prompt: we're reusing our robot from last season in BIOBUZZ, it has 8 motors and 10 servos. any problem?
evals.expected_output: Illegal: BIOBUZZ R503 limits a ROBOT to 8 motors and 8 servos across all configurations used at an event (DECODE allowed 10 servos; TU00 notes the servo max was reduced to 8). Must cut 2 servos.

assertions.name: verdict-illegal-R503
assertions.text: Verdict is illegal, citing R503 with BIOBUZZ text stating 8 motors and 8 servos

assertions.name: no-decode-limit
assertions.text: Does not state or rely on a 10-servo limit as current

assertions.name: citations-verified
assertions.text: Every cited ID passes rules.py verify --season biobuzz-2026-27

evals.name: dashboard-streaming
evals.prompt: we use FTC Dashboard to graph our flywheel velocity. can we leave it running at competition this year (BIOBUZZ)?
evals.expected_output: No. BIOBUZZ R704.D: software may only stream control/debug/telemetry via the FTC Driver Station app; third-party logging/streaming such as FTC Dashboard and FTControl Panels is prohibited; no continuous video stream. (New explicit wording vs DECODE's bandwidth rule.)

assertions.name: cites-R704
assertions.text: Cites R704 and quotes the clause naming FTC Dashboard / FTControl Panels as prohibited

assertions.name: verdict-not-allowed
assertions.text: Verdict: not allowed at events (practice use is not what the rule governs; answer doesn't say it's fine at competition)

evals.name: official-doc-wrong-number
evals.prompt: Team Update 00 says R510 is the allowed motors rule. Is the WATTOS Stingray legal under R510?
evals.expected_output: The WATTOS Stingray 12V DC is legal — it is listed in Table 12-1, referenced by R501 'Only specific motors are allowed'. R510 does not exist in the V1 manual (verify fails); TU00's 'R510' reference corresponds to R501. Cite R501 + [[TABLE:12-1]], not R510.

assertions.name: does-not-cite-R510
assertions.text: The answer does not present R510 as a valid citation; it notes R510 fails verify / doesn't exist in V1

assertions.name: cites-R501-table
assertions.text: Legality grounded in R501 and Table 12-1 read by pointer (manual-tables/biobuzz-2026-27/table-12-1.json), naming the WATTOS Stingray row

evals.name: expansion-physical-not-software
evals.prompt: BIOBUZZ: our arm can reach 32 inches tall but we software-limit it to 28 during matches. legal?
evals.expected_output: Illegal as described: R105.A caps the fully expanded sizing volume at 18 x 24 x 29 in tall and R105.B requires ROBOTS be physically constrained to fit without the use of software. G416 enforces construction limits in-match. (DECODE allowed software-limited vertical expansion — no longer.)

assertions.name: physical-constraint
assertions.text: States the limit must be physical, not software, citing R105 text

assertions.name: traverses-G416
assertions.text: Includes the one-hop in-match rule G416 alongside R105

assertions.name: height-29
assertions.text: Uses 29 in as the height limit from retrieved text, not a DECODE value (18/38 in)

evals.name: herding-is-control
evals.prompt: in BIOBUZZ can we bulldoze a pile of like 6 pollen across the field with the front of our drivetrain? we're not picking them up
evals.expected_output: Likely a violation: G407 — a ROBOT may not simultaneously CONTROL more than 4 SCORING ELEMENTS; the Glossary's CONTROL includes intentionally pushing elements to a desired location (herding). G407's notes distinguish incidental bulldozing/deflection from intentional herding, so the verdict depends on intent; VERBAL WARNING, MAJOR FOUL + YELLOW if STRATEGIC.

assertions.name: uses-glossary-control
assertions.text: Pulls the CONTROL definition (rules.py term CONTROL or equivalent retrieved text) and applies its herding clause

assertions.name: cites-G407
assertions.text: Cites G407 with its limit of 4 and its violation ladder

assertions.name: not-overconfident
assertions.text: Acknowledges the intent/STRATEGIC distinction rather than a flat 'legal because not picked up'

evals.name: figure-only-ambiguous
evals.prompt: which corner is the red GARDEN in for BIOBUZZ, near our alliance area or the opposite side? we're planning auto paths
evals.expected_output: Partly answerable, partly figure-only. The manual text (§9.3) only says GARDENs are ~23 x 2 in zones 'in opposite corners of the FIELD'. The Event Field Setup Guide V1.0 (an official field document, not rule text; recorded in the season yaml's field.tile_positions) places the red GARDEN on tile A1 and the red LOADING ZONE on tile A5. Which physical corner A1 is (which way the A-F / 1-6 grid runs relative to the audience and alliance area) is defined only in the tile-grid figures, which the corpus doesn't store. Answer: tile A1 per the setup guide, orientation from Figure 9-4/9-5 — not inferred from prose.

assertions.name: cites-tile-with-tier
assertions.text: Gives tile A1 for the red GARDEN and labels its source as the Field Setup Guide (field document, not a manual rule)

assertions.name: orientation-figure-only
assertions.text: Does not assert which physical corner/side A1 is from prose; points to the tile-grid figure

evals.name: launch-vs-place-flower
evals.prompt: BIOBUZZ: can our launcher shoot pollen into the top of a FLOWER for points instead of placing it?
evals.expected_output: Ambiguous — worth a Q&A (opens 2026-09-28). §10.5.2 note: 'Placing SCORING ELEMENTS into the top of the FLOWER is the only allowable way to score'; G418 requires entry into the top only; LAUNCH is a defined term. Whether a launched entry counts as placing isn't resolved by text.

assertions.name: retrieves-section-note
assertions.text: Retrieves the §10.5.2 'only allowable way to score' text (rules.py section 10.5.2) and G418

assertions.name: ambiguous-verdict
assertions.text: Verdict is ambiguous with a Q&A recommendation, not a confident legal/illegal

evals.name: prior-season-question
evals.prompt: settle an argument from last season: in DECODE, what was G416 about?
evals.expected_output: Answered from the DECODE corpus with --season decode-2025-26: G416 'LAUNCHING in the LAUNCH ZONE only'. Notes the DECODE corpus is a prior season (freshness WRONG_SEASON is expected and not a reason to refuse an explicitly-DECODE question), and that BIOBUZZ G416 is a different rule (construction limits).

assertions.name: decode-corpus
assertions.text: Uses the DECODE corpus explicitly and quotes G416's DECODE headline

assertions.name: season-labeled
assertions.text: States the answer is about DECODE (prior season) and does not present it as a current rule

evals.name: evergreen-not-unchanged
evals.prompt: R501 has the green asterisk so it's the same motor list as last year right? we have a WATTOS Stingray question from a DECODE-era thread
evals.expected_output: No. In the BIOBUZZ manual the asterisk marks an Evergreen rule — its subject recurs but game-specific details may change (§1.7.1). The BIOBUZZ Table 12-1 adds the WATTOS Stingray; the DECODE table didn't list it. Read the current table.

assertions.name: evergreen-meaning
assertions.text: Explains the asterisk as Evergreen (details can change), citing the manual convention or rules.py asterisk_meaning — not 'unchanged'

assertions.name: reads-current-table
assertions.text: Resolves the answer from the BIOBUZZ Table 12-1 file, not from the DECODE-era thread
